newsitem.title: UK: Dorrell's star wanes in row over Scotland.
newsitem.headline: Dorrell's star wanes in row over Scotland.

text.p: Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell's hopes of one day becoming Conservative party leader suffered a blow on Tuesday when Prime Minister John Major conspicuously declined to say whether Dorrell still had a role as a Conservative spokesman on the constitution.
Dorrell caused a storm on Monday by apparently promising a future Conservative administration would abolish any Scottish parliament set up by a Labour government.
The remark was immediately seized on by opposition parties, which said it was insulting to Scotland and at odds with the views of the ruling party's Scottish Secretary, Michael Forsyth.
Forsyth has said the Conservatives would not reverse any devolution introduced in Scotland by a Labour government.

Major, quizzed on the controversy at a news conference devoted largely to education, was asked whether Dorrell retained the campaigning role on constitutional issues he was given last summer by party chairman Brian Mawhinney.
At the time the appointment angered Conservative right-wingers, including Home Secretary Michael Howard, as well as Forsyth and Welsh Secretary William Hague.

"Constitutional matters are the responsibility of the prime minister, predominantly, and the secretaries of state for Scotland and Wales," the prime minister replied, pointedly omitting any reference to Dorrell.
He also slapped down his health secretary by endorsing Forsyth's views on the difficulty of scrapping a Scottish parliament once it had been established.
"What Michael Forsyth has reiterated time and time again, and I think is undoubted... is that once you have an omelette of that sort it is very difficult to unscramble it." Major said.

Pressed again about Dorrell, Major went on: "Every cabinet minister has an interest of course. If a cabinet minister is answering questions in Wales, he would expect to be asked questions about Wales.
"If he's in Scotland, he would be expected to answer questions about Scotland... but responsibilty for Scotland and Wales rests with the secretaries of state and overall responsibilty rests with me."

Analysts have interpreted recent speeches by Dorrell, notably a sceptical intervention on Europe, as an attempt to jettison any vestiges of his left-leaning past in anticipation of a leadership contest should Major quit if the Conservatives lose the coming election.
Even before Major's news conference, however, commentators said his star was waning.
"Devolution gaffe a setback for Dorrell," was a representative headline in Tuesday's Daily Express.
